verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {applicant_name}, the Applicant herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to my personal knowledge. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Applicant

promptInstructions: Draft an application under Order 11 R.12 / R.14 / R.15 / R.18 read with Section 30 and Section 151 CPC for discovery, production and inspection of documents.
Order 11 R.1 — interrogatories — written questions to be answered on affidavit. Leave of court required (R.2).
Order 11 R.12 — discovery of documents — application to court for direction to opposite party to disclose on affidavit all documents in his possession / power relating to matters in question.
Order 11 R.14 — production — court may order production of documents and inspection at any stage.
Order 11 R.15-19 — inspection of documents referred to in pleadings, affidavits, notices, etc.
Order 11 R.21 — consequences of non-compliance: court may strike out defence / dismiss suit; adverse inference is well-recognised.
Cite M.L. Sethi v. R.P. Kapur (1972) 2 SCC 427 — discovery is to enable parties to know what case other party will set up; not a fishing expedition.
Cite Krishna Lal v. State of Haryana (1980) 3 SCC 159 — relevance and necessity tests for production.
Cite Mathew George v. Cherian Punnan AIR 1990 Ker 67 — specific identification of documents necessary.
Para 1: Reference to main suit, parties, stage.
Para 2: Issues / matters in controversy to which documents relate.
Para 3: Itemised list of documents — each described with: nature, date, parties, subject, approximate description. Avoid vague descriptions like 'all documents relating to'.
Para 4: Relevance and materiality — for each document or category, state how it relates to specific issue and why it is necessary for fair adjudication.
Para 5: Documents are in non-applicant's possession, custody, or power — including documents held by non-applicant's agents, banks, accountants.
Para 6: Applicant does not have copies and cannot reasonably obtain them.

Para 7: Documents not protected by legal privilege under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 — note BSA replaces Indian Evidence Act 1872. Relevant privileges: S.132 BSA (privileged communication between spouses), S.134 (state communications), S.136 (no person to be compelled to produce title-deeds), S.139 (professional communications with legal advisers — replaces S.126 IEA).
Para 8: Banking secrecy — bank documents may require notice / S.4 Bankers' Books Evidence Act for certified entries.
Para 9: Documents not protected by RTI exemptions, official secrets, or other statutory immunity.
Para 10: Previous demand — if applicant served notice on opposite party requesting voluntary production, note demand and any refusal.
Para 11: Adverse inference under O.11 R.21 — refusal or failure to produce relevant documents in own custody invites adverse presumption.

Where Commercial Courts Act applies (commercial dispute >= Rs.3 lakh): Schedule of CCA replaces Order 11 with detailed mandatory disclosure regime (Order XI of CCA Schedule) — mandatory affidavit of disclosure within 30 days of WS; further discovery on application; non-compliance carries serious consequences.
For document held by third party (not opposite party): use Order 16 R.6 (subpoena duces tecum) and S.30(c) CPC — different application.
Where document held by government / public office: S.137-138 BSA (formerly S.123-124 IEA) — state privilege; production by way of certified copy if not privileged.
Inspection facility — usually at advocate's office under supervision; copies on payment of cost.
Interrogatories must be specific, relate to matters in question, not be in nature of cross-examination, not be oppressive.
Affidavit in support is mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.
